'''Richard John Blaikie''' (born 25 August 1965) is a physicist who works in the field of nano-scale optics. He was Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Enterprise) at the [[University of Otago]] until  June 2025, and is now Professor Emeritus at the [[Department_of_Physics_at_the_University_of_Otago|Department of Physics]].

==Early life==
Blaikie was born in 1965 and attended [[Kaikorai Valley College]] in [[Dunedin]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Former police boss keen to track down KVC alumni |url=http://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/247521/former-police-boss-keen-track-down-kvc-alumni |accessdate=8 August 2015 |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=28 February 2013}}</ref> He studied at the University of Otago (1984–1987) and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] (Hons) in physics. He won a [[Ernest Rutherford|Rutherford]] Memorial Scholarship to attend the [[University of Cambridge]] (1988–1992), where he received a PhD in physics in 1992.

==Academic career==
After a year at the Hitachi Cambridge Laboratory, he took a position as a lecturer at the [[University of Canterbury]].<ref name="Otago Uni bio">{{cite web |title=University appoints next Research Deputy Vice-Chancellor |url=http://www.otago.ac.nz/news/news/otago018015.html |publisher=[[University of Otago]] |accessdate=8 August 2015 |date=10 May 2011}}</ref> He was at Canterbury from February 1994 to November 2011, and he was made a professor during that time. In 2001, he was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="MacDiarmid bio" />

When the [[MacDiarmid Institute for Advanced Materials and Nanotechnology]] was formed in 2002, he was appointed Deputy Director under Professor [[Paul Callaghan]]. When Callaghan retired in 2008, Blaikie was appointed Director.<ref name="MacDiarmid bio" /> During his tenure, the institute received a bequest of [[New Zealand dollar|NZ$]]1&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Donor gives MacDiarmid Institute $1m for nanotechnology |url=http://www.odt.co.nz/news/national/68571/donor-gives-victoria-uni-1m-nanotechnology |accessdate=8 August 2015 |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=5 August 2009}}</ref> Blaikie stepped down from the MacDiarmid Institute half way through 2011 when he received his appointment as Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Enterprise) at the University of Otago. He took up the role in December 2011, succeeding [[Harlene Hayne]].<ref name="MacDiarmid bio">{{cite web|title=New role for Prof Richard Blaikie|url=http://www.macdiarmid.ac.nz/new-role-for-prof-richard-blaikie/|publisher=[[MacDiarmid Institute for Advanced Materials and Nanotechnology]]|accessdate=8 August 2015|date=18 May 2011}}</ref><ref name="ODT new VC" /> He also holds a chair in physics.<ref name="ODT new VC">{{cite news |title=Physicist appointed |url=http://www.odt.co.nz/campus/university-otago/160548/physicist-appointed |accessdate=8 August 2015 |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=16 May 2011}}</ref>

Blaikie received the [[T. K. Sidey Medal]] in 2001, set up by the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] as an award for outstanding scientific research.<ref>{{cite web |title=Background of the Medal |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/sidey-medal/background/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of New Zealand]] |accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Recipients |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/sidey-medal/recipients/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of New Zealand]] |accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref> In 2011, Blaikie was elected fellow of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Otago researchers made fellows of Royal Society |url=http://www.odt.co.nz/campus/university-otago/185012/otago-researchers-made-fellows-royal-society |accessdate=8 August 2015 |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=3 November 2011}}</ref> In 2013, Blaikie received the [[Hector Memorial Medal]] from the Royal Society "for his fundamental and wide-ranging contributions to the field of nano-optics, showing that light can be manipulated at scales much smaller than its wavelength and providing a world-first demonstration of a controversial [[superlens]] system using subwavelength techniques."<ref>{{cite web |title=Medals awarded to top New Zealand researchers |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/2013/11/27/medals-awarded-to-top-new-zealand-researchers-3/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of New Zealand]] |accessdate=7 August 2015 | date=27 November 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Recipients |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of New Zealand]] |accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=NZ's highest science honour awarded|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11163781|accessdate=9 August 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=27 November 2013}}</ref> The national ceremony for a range of Royal Society awards were held in the [[Dunedin Town Hall]] on 27 November 2013.<ref>{{cite news |title=High honours for three Otago researchers |url=http://www.odt.co.nz/campus/university-otago/283247/high-honours-three-otago-researchers |accessdate=9 August 2015 |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=28 November 2013 |first=John |last=Gibb}}</ref> In 2015, Blaikie was awarded the [[Thomson Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Thomson Medal]] for science leadership.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Spotlight on top
